correction.text: shape unchanged, drawn from 973 when Tailapa II took the Rashtrakuta capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 973-979: Cliopatria's first row starts in 980 but the page makes the Chalukyas sovereign from 973 ('Vassal of the Rashtrakutas (957-973), then sovereign (973-1184)'; 'In 973, seeing confusion in the Rashtrakuta empire after a successful invasion of their capital'). The 980 shape is drawn back to 973; the Rashtrakuta dossier gives the matching 973 loss and keeps only Indra IV's remnant on the Mysore plateau.

731,530 km2 for 980-989. The page gives no area (its only map caption is 'Greatest extent of the Western Chalukya Empire, 1121 AD'), so no infobox comparison is possible. The shape covers all of Maharashtra and most of Karnataka and Telangana; the page names no boundary for these years. unverified: page budget. A gap-filler should check the Mysore-plateau strip in the south (about 91 of its 298 cells): the Chola dossier has Gangapadi annexed by the Cholas in 998 and Indra IV's remnant there to 982. Satyashraya page (opened 2026-10-19) says nothing of Gangavadi, Nolambavadi or the Mysore plateau; the strip stays unverified.

753,172 km2: +22,000 km2 on the 980 shape, almost all in a strip at 12.7-13.8 N, 75.4-78.1 E (southern Karnataka). The page is silent on any 990 gain; the Paramara page records that after Tailapa's defeat and killing of Munja (994-998) the Paramaras 'lost territory south of the Narmada', which is already inside this shape. unverified: page budget.
754,152 km2, the largest of the row (+1,000 km2 on 990). Satyashraya's reign; the page has no area and no boundary for these years. unverified: page budget.

602,424 km2: Cliopatria removes 608 cells (12.7-17.5 N, 73.2-80.2 E: southern Karnataka and the Andhra country, 20 percent of the shape) from 1010 to 1033. The page dates the Chola invasion of 1007 ('In 1007 Chola crown-prince Rajendra Chola I invaded Western Chalukyas and had a battle') and further battles 'around c. 1020-21' but names no land lost, so the 1010 loss in the ledger is a confidence-1 bridge. Cliopatria returns the same strip in 1034 and removes it again in 1040; no page opened explains the oscillation. unverified: page budget. Repair of 2026-10-19: upper Konkan (the Mumbai 100 km disc, 67 of whose 68 cells lie in this shape) is Chalukya to 1019 and drops out in 1020-1054 (keyframes below, ledger loss 1020 to paramara-dynasty).

New keyframe 1020-1033: 'Bhoja invaded and captured Konkana sometime between 1018 and 1020 CE' (Bhoja page; his 1020 inscription celebrates the Konkana-Grahana Vijaya Parva); 'By the end of his reign, Bhoja had lost this territory to the Chalukyas of Kalyani' (1055). The 1010 shape without the Mumbai 100 km disc.

738,006 km2 for 1034-1039: the southern strip of 1010 is back (521 cells) and the shape reaches 82.4 E (the Vengi coast). The page is silent on 1034; the Chola dossier has civil war in Vengi from 1031 and a Chola expedition in 1035. Kept as Cliopatria draws it; unverified: page budget. Upper Konkan is out until 1054 (repair of 2026-10-19). Jayasimha II page: Western Chalukya invasion of Vengi 1031, Kalidindi 1032, Vijayawada and Vengi conquered 1037.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1034 shape without upper Konkan; the years are 1034-1039
shape unchanged apart from upper Konkan, which is out; the years are 1040-1054

keyframe_review.note: 602,424 km2, the shape of 1010 (less the 68-cell Konkan disc until 1054): the base shape of the Kalyani period, 1040-1054. Konkan returns in 1055 (next keyframe); Vengi is added from 1093 (the Vikramaditya VI page has Vengi under Chalukya rule 'from 1093 to 1099').

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1040 shape, with upper Konkan back; the years are 1055-1092

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1055-1092: 'By the end of his reign, Bhoja had lost this territory to the Chalukyas of Kalyani' (Bhoja page; 1055 is the last year of the reign). The 1040 shape applies as the base until Vengi is added in 1093.

correction.text: shape unchanged; the years are 1093-1099, not 1094-1098

keyframe_review.note: 639,275 km2: the 1040 shape plus Vengi (the Andhra coast to 82.4 E). The Vikramaditya VI page: 'Vengi came under his rule again from 1093 to 1099' and the Western Chalukya page 'Vengi was under his control from c. 1093 to 1099'. Cliopatria's 1094-1098 should read 1093-1099. The 1088 conquest of 'parts of Vengi' (Kollipakei-7000) is in the ledger.
602,424 km2, the base shape again. With Vengi held to 1099 inclusive on the page, this shape begins in 1100.

600,039 km2: the base shape with the southern tip trimmed (lat 14.09) and 62 more cells in Gujarat (Lata: the Vikramaditya VI page has 'He invaded Lata (modern Gujarat)' before 1088). It holds 1111-1117; the page has Vengi under Chalukya rule again from 1118, so 1118-1125 takes the shape of the 1126 row (new keyframe 1118). Hoysala Vishnuvardhana's 1116 Talakad victory and the Hoysala annexation of Gangavadi took place in Chola, not Chalukya, land.

New keyframe 1118-1125: the page has Vengi 'conquered and came under his rule from 1118 to 1124' (the Western Chalukya page: 'reconquered in c. 1118 and held it till 1124'), so the shape with Vengi starts eight years before Cliopatria's 1126 row.

636,192 km2 for 1126-1138, the base shape plus Vengi. The Vikramaditya VI page has 'By 1133 Vikrama Chola was able to re-capture Vengi from Vikramaditya VI's mild son Someshvara III' and the Chola dossier dates the Chola gain to 1133 (Battle of Godavari), so the Vengi shape ends in 1133, and 1134-1138 takes the base shape (new keyframe 1134). The Western Chalukya page's 'held it till 1124' disagrees with 1133; the later date is used because it is the one the Chola side confirms.
New keyframe 1134-1138: Vengi is lost in 1133, but Cliopatria keeps the Vengi shape to 1138; the base shape of the 1139 row applies from 1134.

599,818 km2 for 1139-1176. The page dates the Kalachuri capture of Kalyani to 1157 ('captured Kalyani and occupied it for the next twenty years'), a year when the Chalukya capital and its district passed to Bijjala II; the shape is kept whole and the occupation is drawn as hatching from the ledger (occupation_start 1157). Prola's Kakatiya victory of 1149 names no land. The Kalachuri page puts Bijjala's independence in 1162 and the Chalukya recovery 'after 1181'. Repair of 2026-10-19: the shape holds to 1162; Telangana leaves in 1163.

New keyframe 1163-1176: 'They assumed sovereignty under Rudradeva in 1163 CE by suppressing other Chalukya subordinates in the Telangana region' (Kakatiya page). Cliopatria's Kakatiya row begins in 1177, fourteen years later; the Chalukya shape without Telangana applies from 1163. The Kalachuri hold of Kalyani (1157-1183) stays a hatched occupation in the ledger.

510,696 km2 for 1177-1187: Cliopatria removes 330 cells of Telangana (the Kakatiya country, whose row begins in 1177) and a little of Maharashtra. No page opened dates the Kakatiya break-away (the Chalukya page has only 'defeated by the Kakatiya king Prola in 1149'), so the 1177 loss is a confidence-1 bridge. The Seuna page: Bhillama V 'conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani, and declared himself a sovereign ruler' in 1187; the Western Chalukya page puts the end at 1189 ('drove Someshvara IV into exile in Banavasi') and its infobox at 1184. 1187 is kept as the end year.

region.text: the Rashtrakuta core, Manyakheta and the Deccan, taken by Tailapa II

ledger.note: 973: Tailapa II makes the Chalukyas sovereign at the Rashtrakuta capital Manyakheta. The page's status line reads 'Vassal of the Rashtrakutas (957-973), then sovereign (973-1184)' and 'In 973, seeing confusion in the Rashtrakuta empire after a successful invasion of their capital'; the infobox 'Established: 957' is the date of the earliest record, 'dated 957, during the rule of Tailapa II'. The page does not give the land; the shape is Cliopatria's 980 shape.

region.text: the southern marches of the Chalukya kingdom, north of Gangavadi up to the Tungabhadra, where the Chola invasions of 1007 and c. 1020-21 fell (the Chola dossier's Ratta Padi zone; the page names no place)

ledger.note: 1007: the Cholas invade the Chalukya country. 'In 1007 Chola crown-prince Rajendra Chola I invaded Western Chalukyas and had a battle'; the inscription claims 'an army of 900,000 soldiers'. The Chola dossier opens the Ratta Padi campaign in 1003 on the Rajaraja I page, which this dossier did not open. The zone is the Chola dossier's; the page names no place.

region.text: Lata proper, southern Gujarat: the Vadodara and Surat discs without the northern margin (59 cells at 21.2-23.4 N, 72.1-73.7 E) that Cliopatria's 1111-1303 Chaulukya shapes keep and that lies in Gujarat proper

ledger.note: By 1007: the Lata region passes to the Western Chalukyas. 'Sometime before 1007 CE, the Lata region was captured by the Chalukyas of Kalyani led by Satyashraya.' The page gives no year for the capture; it also says Lata 'was under Chaulukya suzerainty' in the 990s. Recorded in the Chaulukya dossier as the loss and here as the Chalukya gain. Cliopatria draws no Lata in the Chalukya shape until 1111. Satyashraya page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Satyashraya led an expedition to Gujarat, defeated Mularaja' and there was 'rebellion against the Lata Chalukya chief Barapa in the Gujarat province' (no years); reign 997-1008. Lata is Lata proper (the Vadodara 120 km and Surat 80 km discs without the 59 northern-margin cells that Cliopatria keeps Chaulukya in 1111-1303): one region for chaulukya-dynasty, paramara-dynasty and this dossier (repair of 2026-10-19).

region.text: Lata proper, southern Gujarat: the Vadodara and Surat discs without the northern margin (59 cells at 21.2-23.4 N, 72.1-73.7 E) that Cliopatria's 1111-1303 Chaulukya shapes keep and that lies in Gujarat proper

ledger.note: c. 1008: Durlabharaja takes Lata back. 'He invaded the Lata region, and defeated the Lata Chalukya ruler Kirtiraja' (c. 1008). The page adds that Kirtiraja regained control 'within a short time', undated, and was defeated by Bhoja c. 1018, so the hold may have been brief. Confidence 1 (was 2): the Chaulukya page dates Durlabharaja's accession (c. 1008), not the Lata campaign; matches chaulukya-dynasty /ledger gain 1008. Lata is Lata proper (the Vadodara 120 km and Surat 80 km discs without the 59 northern-margin cells that Cliopatria keeps Chaulukya in 1111-1303): one region for chaulukya-dynasty, paramara-dynasty and this dossier (repair of 2026-10-19).

region.text: the strip of southern Karnataka and the Andhra country (12.7-17.5 N, 73.2-80.2 E) that Cliopatria's 1010 shape drops

ledger.note: c. 1010 (bridge): the southern Deccan leaves the Chalukya shape. Cliopatria removes 608 cells (southern Karnataka and the Andhra country) from 1010 to 1033; the page's 1007 invasion and c. 1020-21 battles with the Cholas are the only related sentences and name no land. Page silent on the year and the land; the Chola dossier records no matching gain, only Gangapadi annexed in 998 and the Ratta Padi war. Pages reread 2026-10-19: Satyashraya page: Rajendra 'captured Donur in the Bijapur region, Banavasi, parts of the Raichur Doab' (no year) and 'Satyashraya annexed Andhra province from Cholas'; Jayasimha II page: he 'had marched south of the Tungabhadra River and occupied Bellary, the Raichur Doab and perhaps part of Gangavadi' and 'reconquered Gangawadi and Raichur from Cholas after the Battle of Maski' (no years; Maski c. 1021 is called exaggerated) and 'the Tungabhadra River remained the tacit border'. None of these sentences gives a year or an outline, so the 1010 step stays a bridge.

1018-1020: Bhoja captures upper Konkan. 'Bhoja invaded and captured Konkana sometime between 1018 and 1020 CE' from the Shilahara king Arikesari, a Chalukya feudatory (Satyashraya page: 'Satyashraya however subdued the Shilahara King Aparajita of the northern Konkan'); 'His 1020 CE inscription states that he organized a Konkana-Grahana Vijaya Parva'. Added in the repair of 2026-10-19 (reviewer finding): the keyframes drew Konkan from 1010 while paramara-dynasty held it for 1020-1055, and /ledger gain 1055 took it back with no loss. Mirror: paramara-dynasty /ledger gain 1020 (counterpart now this state). Disagreement: the Jayasimha II page has him 'to recover all his northern territories by c.1024' and the Western Chalukya page 'Jayasimha II subdued the Paramara of central India' (c. 1024), while the Bhoja page has Konkan lost only 'by the end of his reign'; the Bhoja page is the specific one and is followed.

region.text: the southern marches of the Chalukya kingdom, north of Gangavadi up to the Tungabhadra, where the Chola invasions of 1007 and c. 1020-21 fell (the Chola dossier's Ratta Padi zone; the page names no place)

ledger.note: c. 1020-21: the Chola wars on the southern marches end. 'fought many battles with the Cholas in the south around c. 1020-21.' The page gives no treaty; the Chola dossier closes the Ratta Padi war in 1020 with Maski.

region.text: the strip dropped in 1010 plus the Vengi coast, as Cliopatria's 1034 shape

ledger.note: 1034 (bridge): the southern strip and the Vengi coast return to the Chalukya shape (521 more cells, to 82.4 E). Page silent: no sentence of the Western Chalukya page covers 1034; Jayasimha II is named there only for the c. 1020-21 Chola battles and the c. 1024 Paramara campaign. Counterpart is the Chola Empire by reading of the Chola dossier (Vengi civil war from 1031). Jayasimha II page (opened 2026-10-19): 'the Karnataka or the Western Chalukya invasion of Vengi may be assigned to A.D. 1031', the battle of Kalidindi 'in the succeeding year', 'Jayasimha II conquered Vijayawada Fort after defeating Cholas in the Battle of Vijayawada (1037 AD)' and 'He conquered Vengi in 1037 AD and placed Vijayaditya on Vengi throne'. These dates explain the Vengi-coast part of Cliopatria's 1034 shape in 1031-1037 but not its year or the southern strip, so the event stays a confidence-1 bridge.

region.text: the strip and the Vengi coast that Cliopatria's 1034 shape adds

ledger.note: 1040 (bridge): the 1034 additions leave the shape again, 136,000 km2. Page silent for these years; the Koppam war of 1052-1054 is the next dated event. Jayasimha II page: 'this period saw Vengi fall firmly into the hands of the Cholas' (no year).
c. 1042: Someshvara I moves the Chalukya capital to Kalyani. 'moved the Chalukya capital to Kalyani in c. 1042.'

region.text: Rattamandalam and Kolhapur, where Rajadhiraja plundered and Rajendra II set up his pillar

ledger.note: 1052: Rajadhiraja's second invasion. 'In 1052, he led a second expedition into the Chalukya territories'; he 'plundered the province of Rattamandalam'; the Chalukya army was beaten at Koppam on 28 May 1052 (the infobox; some sources say 1054) and 'Rajendra II ... erected a victory pillar at Kolhapur'. A raid, not an annexation: the zone is the Kolhapur country the page names.

1052: the Koppam campaign ends in a Chola victory without annexation. Infobox: 'Chola victory', 'Date 28 May 1052'; 'Rajadhiraja I lost his life in the battlefield'. The page names no territorial change and no peace.

By 1055: the Chalukyas take upper Konkan from the Paramaras. 'By the end of his reign, Bhoja had lost this territory to the Chalukyas of Kalyani' (Bhoja page; 1055 is the last year of the reign). Cliopatria's Chalukya shape holds the Konkan from 980; it is dropped here for 1020-1054 (ledger loss 1020) and returns with this event's loss.

1058: the Chalukyas plunder Malwa. 'the Chalukyas plundered the important Paramara cities, including Dhara' (Chalukya inscriptions, 1058-1067). The Paramara page puts Someshvara I's invasion earlier, 'sometime after 1042 CE', and has Dhara sacked then; 1058 is the first year the Bhoja page dates.

region.text: the Vengi country around Vijayawada, where the 1068 battle was fought

ledger.note: 1066: the Chola frontier war reopens. 'In 1066, Vikramaditya VI, Son of Someshwara I had invaded the Chola Empire'; the next dated event is 'the Battle of Vijayawada which was fought in 1068 between Someshvara I and Chola Emperor Virarajendra Chola'. The page names Vijayawada, not the limits of the zone.
1067: the plunder of the Paramara cities ends. The last year of the Bhoja page's 1058-1067 plunder; no treaty is named. Malwa returned to the Paramaras, whose Cliopatria shape is unbroken.

1068: the Battle of Vijayawada. 'The Battle of Vijayawada which was fought in 1068 between Someshvara I and Chola Emperor Virarajendra Chola'; Someshvara I died in April 1068. The page names no result and no land.

region.text: Kanchi, the Pallava and Chola city, captured in 1085

ledger.note: 1085: Vikramaditya VI takes Kanchi. 'He invaded and captured Kanchi in 1085 and held it for a few years.' Held without annexation: hatched over the Chola capital region.

1088: Vikramaditya VI takes parts of Vengi. 'He managed to conquer parts of Vengi in 1088.' 'He held the Kollipakei-7000 province of Vengi for many years.' Recorded as a contest (repair of 2026-10-19, reviewer finding): the first version gained the whole Vengi union (218 cells, 55,000 km2) in 1088, but the page says only 'parts of Vengi', no keyframe drew Vengi before 1093, and /ledger gain 1093 took the same land again with no loss. The page does not place the Kollipakei-7000 province; Kolanupaka (17.69 N 79.03 E, Telangana, the reviewer's suggestion) is not tied to it by the Kolanupaka page and its 57-cell disc lies inside Cliopatria's Western Chalukya shape of 1040-1176 and 0 cells in Chola Vengi, so it cannot be the new land. Vengi is the zone fought over until the page's 'from 1093 to 1099'. Mirror to add in chola-empire: contest 1088-1093.

c. 1089 (bridge): Kanchi leaves Chalukya hands. 'held it for a few years'; 'Although Kulottunga I subsequently recovered the region, it was later regained by Vikramaditya.' The page gives no year for the loss, so 1089 (four years after 1085) is a confidence-1 bridge.
1093: the contest of 1088 ends with the conquest. 'Vengi came under his rule again from 1093 to 1099.' The page gives no battle for 1088-1092.
1093: Vengi again. 'Vengi came under his rule again from 1093 to 1099.' The Western Chalukya page: he defeated Kulottunga I 'in the battle of Vengi in 1093'. Cliopatria's Vengi shape starts in 1094.
1099: Vengi lost. The same page: Vengi under Chalukya rule 'from 1093 to 1099'.

intersect.text: Lata proper, southern Gujarat: the Vadodara and Surat discs without the northern margin (59 cells at 21.2-23.4 N, 72.1-73.7 E) that Cliopatria's 1111-1303 Chaulukya shapes keep and that lies in Gujarat proper

region.text: the southern Lata cells (63 cells of southern Gujarat) that Cliopatria's 1111 shape adds

ledger.note: 1111 (bridge): 63 more Gujarat cells (Lata proper) enter the Chalukya shape. Cliopatria's year; the Vikramaditya VI page says only that he 'invaded Lata (modern Gujarat), plundered and burnt the royal capital of the Gurjara Chalukya King Karna' without a year, and the Jayasimha Siddharaja page that Kalyani Chalukya records claim he 'crossed the Narmada River, and conquered the Lata and Gurjara regions' (no year; historians consider it unsupported). Counterpart changed from chaulukya-dynasty to 'nobody' in the repair of 2026-10-19: the Chaulukya dossier now has Lata lost in 1077 (to Trivikramapala), so the cells were nobody's in 1110. Lata is Lata proper (the Vadodara 120 km and Surat 80 km discs without the 59 northern-margin cells that Cliopatria keeps Chaulukya in 1111-1303): one region for chaulukya-dynasty, paramara-dynasty and this dossier (repair of 2026-10-19).

c. 1118: Vengi a third time. 'conquered and came under his rule from 1118 to 1124'; the Western Chalukya page: 'reconquered in c. 1118 and held it till 1124'. The Chola dossier records the loss in c. 1118.

c. 1122: the Hoysalas accept Chalukya suzerainty. After battles at 'Goa, Kannegala, Halasur and Hosavidu' (c.1117-1122) Vishnuvardhana 'had to accept Chalukya suzerainty'. The page dates the battles to c.1117-1122 and gives no later year, so 1122 is the last year of the war. Vishnuvardhana had annexed Gangavadi from the Cholas after Talakad in 1116.

1126 (bridge): Vikramaditya VI dies and the Hoysala tie lapses. 'after Vikramaditya VI's death in 1126' (Western Chalukya page). No page opened says when the Hoysalas ceased to acknowledge the Chalukyas; the year is a confidence-1 bridge. Cliopatria draws the Hoysalas as their own row throughout. Vishnuvardhana page (opened 2026-10-19): he 'had to accept, for the time being, subordination to the Chalukya throne'; 'Majumdar claims Vishnuvardhana controlled areas in the Krishna river region even around c.1131' while performing a ceremony 'despite his nominal subordination to the Chalukyas'; 'After the death of Vikarmaditya VI, the Hoysala monarch re-captured Hanagal, Uchchangi and Bankapura by c.1140'. The nominal tie may therefore run to c. 1131; no page ends it, so 1126 stays.

1133: the Cholas retake Vengi. 'By 1133 Vikrama Chola was able to re-capture Vengi from Vikramaditya VI's mild son Someshvara III.' The Western Chalukya page's footnote has Vengi held 'till 1124'; the Chola dossier dates the Chola gain to 1133 (Battle of Godavari).

1157: the Kalachuris take Kalyani. 'In 1157 the Kalachuris of Kalyanis under Bijjala II captured Kalyani and occupied it for the next twenty years.' The Kalachuri page puts Bijjala's independence in 1162 and the Kalachuri peak at 1156-1181.

region.text: Telangana and the margins that Cliopatria's 1177 shape drops

ledger.note: 1163: Telangana leaves the Chalukya shape for the Kakatiyas. Kakatiya page (opened 2026-10-19): 'They assumed sovereignty under Rudradeva in 1163 CE by suppressing other Chalukya subordinates in the Telangana region'; 'It was during Prataparudra's reign, in 1163, that the Kakatiyas declared an end to their status' as feudatories; 'The 1149 Sanigaram inscription of Prola II is the last known record of the Kakatiyas as vassals'; 'The 1163 Anumakonda inscription ... is the earliest known record' of sovereignty. Moved from 1177 (confidence 1, Cliopatria's year for the Kakatiya row) in the repair of 2026-10-19. The land is the 330 Telangana cells Cliopatria drops in 1177; the page names no boundary (region is my reading, confidence 2).

1183: the Kalachuri hold on Kalyani ends. The page: 'their rule ended in 1183 when the last Chalukya scion Someshvara IV tried to recapture Kalyani' (also 'the next twenty years' from 1157, i.e. to 1177). The Kalachuri page: 'after 1181 CE, the Chalukyas gradually retrieved the territory'.

1187: Bhillama V takes Kalyani. 'conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani, and declared himself a sovereign ruler.' The page does not describe a battle against the Chalukya armies. The Western Chalukya page has Someshvara IV driven into exile at Banavasi in 1189.

region.text: the rump held at the end, divided among the Seunas, Hoysalas and Kakatiyas

ledger.note: 1187: the Western Chalukya Empire ends. Seuna page: Kalyani conquered in 1187. The Western Chalukya page has 'the dynasty was ended by the Seuna rulers who drove Someshvara IV into exile' at Banavasi in 1189, and its infobox says 1184; the Hoysalas and Kakatiyas are its other infobox successors.

wars.name: Chola invasions of the Western Chalukya country

zones.text: the southern marches of the Chalukya kingdom, north of Gangavadi up to the Tungabhadra, where the Chola invasions of 1007 and c. 1020-21 fell (the Chola dossier's Ratta Padi zone; the page names no place)

wars.outcome: Chola invasions of 1007 and c. 1020-21; the page names no territorial result. The Chola dossier records the Ratta Padi war of 1003-1020 ending at Maski.
wars.note: Dated by the Western Chalukya page: 'In 1007 Chola crown-prince Rajendra Chola I invaded Western Chalukyas and had a battle' and 'fought many battles with the Cholas in the south around c. 1020-21'.

wars.name: Western Chalukya-Paramara wars
wars.outcome: c. 1024: 'Jayasimha II subdued the Paramara of central India' (Western Chalukya page); after 1042 Someshvara I invaded Malwa and sacked Dhara (Paramara and Bhoja pages); the Chalukyas plundered Paramara cities in 1058-1067. No annexation is recorded.
wars.note: The 1058-1067 span is the Bhoja page's; the contest events use it.

wars.name: Battle of Koppam
wars.outcome: Chola victory (infobox, 28 May 1052; the page also gives 1054 and 1052 'according to Sen'); Rajadhiraja was killed and Rajendra II crowned himself on the field and set up a pillar at Kolhapur. No land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Vijayawada
wars.outcome: Vikramaditya VI invaded the Chola Empire in 1066 and Someshvara I fought Virarajendra Chola at Vijayawada in 1068; the page names no result.

wars.name: Vikramaditya VI's wars for Kanchi and Vengi
wars.outcome: Kanchi captured in 1085 and held a few years; parts of Vengi contested from 1088; Vengi held 1093-1099 and 1118-1124 (the Chola side takes it back by 1133).

wars.name: Hoysala-Chalukya war
wars.outcome: After the Hoysala victory over the Cholas at Talakad in 1116, battles at 'Goa, Kannegala, Halasur and Hosavidu' (c.1117-1122) ended with Vishnuvardhana accepting Chalukya suzerainty.
wars.note: No Chalukya land changed hands; Gangavadi was Chola land.

wars.name: Chalukya-Kakatiya war of 1149
wars.outcome: The Chalukya ruler 'was defeated by the Kakatiya king Prola in 1149'; no land is named.

wars.name: Kalachuri usurpation of Kalyani
wars.outcome: Bijjala II captured Kalyani in 1157; the Chalukyas, under Someshvara IV, recovered it from 1181-1183.

wars.name: Seuna conquest of Kalyani
wars.outcome: Bhillama V conquered Kalyani in 1187; Someshvara IV was driven into exile at Banavasi in 1189 and the dynasty ended.
wars.note: The Seuna page has the Yadava-Hoysala border on the Krishna and Malaprabha after the Hoysala victory at Soratur in the late 1180s.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is given by any page opened; the Tungabhadra and Krishna lines against the Hoysalas and Seunas are described but not surveyed, and the Narmada is the rough northern limit. Vengi, Kanchi and Kalyani are held for named spans only.

notes:
Settled from pages: founding 973, the capital move to Kalyani c. 1042, Vengi 1093-1099 and 1118-1124 (to 1133), Kanchi 1085, the Kalachuri hold of Kalyani 1157-1183, the end in 1187 (Seuna page).
Not settled: (1) Cliopatria oscillates the southern strip (12.7-17.5 N): out 1010-1033, back 1034-1039, out from 1040; no page opened explains it (the Chalukya page names no land for the Chola wars), so all three are confidence-1 bridges. A gap-filler should open 'Jayasimha II (Western Chalukya)', 'Someshvara I' and the Chola dossier's Rajaraja/Rajendra pages. (2) Cliopatria shapes 980-1009 include the Mysore-plateau strip (about 91 of 298 'Mysore (region)' cells) which the Chola dossier gives to the Western Gangas and then the Cholas (Gangapadi annexed 998). (3) The Lata timeline is settled in the repair paragraph below. (4) End date: Seuna page 1187 (kept), Western Chalukya text 1189, infobox 1184. (5) Kalachuri occupation of Kalyani 1157-1183: the page also says 'the next twenty years', i.e. to 1177; 1183 is the page's own end of Kalachuri rule. (6) The Chola dossier opens the Ratta Padi war in 1003 and closes it at Maski in 1020 from the Rajaraja I and Rajendra I pages; this dossier's 1007-1021 is from the Western Chalukya page only. (7) Counterpart states without a dossier: kalachuris-of-kalyani. Name needed in the gazetteer: Basavakalyan (Kalyani), 17.87 N 76.95 E. The page budget (5) was spent on: Western Chalukya Empire, Battle of Koppam, Vikramaditya VI, Seuna dynasty, Kalachuris of Kalyani; the Chaulukya, Paramara and Bhoja pages were opened for the Chaulukya and Paramara dossiers and are cited here for the Lata and Dhara events. Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola-Chalukya_wars (not found).

Repair 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review of sa-03-f, verdict fail). (1) Vengi 1088: now a contest 1088-1093 (counterpart chola-empire), not a gain of the whole 218-cell union: the Vikramaditya VI page says only 'parts of Vengi' and 'the Kollipakei-7000 province' and does not place it; the Kolanupaka page (coordinates only) does not tie Kolanupaka to Kollipaka, and a disc there lies wholly inside the base shape, so the reviewer's reading cannot be the new land (I disagree with the suggestion to draw it as a gain there). Kolanupaka (17.69 N 79.03 E) is a gazetteer name for whoever places the province. (2) Konkan: loss c. 1020 to paramara-dynasty (confidence 2) and keyframes 1020-1033, 1034-1039 and 1040-1054 without it; 1055 gain kept. (3) Lata: 1007 gain and 1008 loss use Lata proper (shared region); the 1111 gain of 63 cells comes from 'nobody' because chaulukya-dynasty lost Lata in 1077 and keeps only the northern margin, which is not Lata proper. (4) Telangana moved from 1177 to 1163 (Kakatiya page: sovereignty under Rudradeva in 1163; confidence 2), with a new keyframe 1163-1176; Cliopatria's Kakatiya row starts 1177, so the kakatiya-dynasty dossier should start no later than 1163. (5) Thin items looked at: the southern strip (1010, 1034, 1040) is still unexplained although the Jayasimha II page dates the Vengi invasion to 1031, Kalidindi 1032 and the conquest of Vengi to 1037, and has the Raichur Doab and Gangavadi retaken after Maski (undated); the Satyashraya page has nothing on Gangavadi or the Mysore plateau; the Kulothunga I page has no sentence on Kanchi (1085-1089) and the Vishnuvardhana page no end of the Hoysala vassalage (nominal subordination c. 1131; recaptures by c. 1140). Mirrors the Chola dossier (sa-03-e) lacks: contest 1088-1093 and the 1093 and 1099 Vengi changes, the Kanchi occupation 1085-1089, the 1010, 1034 and 1040 steps. Counterparts needing a dossier: kalachuris-of-kalyani (as before), paramara-dynasty is a dossier, kakatiya-dynasty and hoysala-kingdom are group sa-03.
